Detection only: every request is inspected and what the rules find is logged, and the request passes - the first mode of a new site, to see what the rules would refuse before they refuse it. Blocking: a request the rules judge an attack is refused with 403.

Each site is published here: its requests end on this firewall, ModSecurity inspects them with the OWASP Core Rule Set, and Apache passes them on to the site's backend. A site reached through a port forward instead never meets these rules.
Enabled sites with a certificate are served over HTTPS: give an HTTPS port, or take their certificates away.
Enabled sites without a certificate are served over plain HTTP: give an HTTP port, or each of them a certificate.

For an https:// backend: its certificate must be signed by an authority of this firewall's trust store and be valid for the site's host names, not for the name or address written in Backend - the name the browser asked for is passed on, and asked of the backend (SNI). A backend whose certificate names only itself: turn this off. Off: any certificate is taken - only for a server on a network you trust.
